proposal.utterance: In BFO terms, what is an unjust command?

entities.label: UnjustCommand
entities.rationale: A command (directive, order, norm) is a piece of information content that can be encoded in multiple physical substrates (spoken, written, signaled) — fitting BFO's generically dependent continuant (GDC). The 'unjust' qualifier is an evaluative quality that inheres in the bearer of the command-as-GDC, modeled separately as a quality. The command itself is the GDC; its injustice is a specifically dependent continuant (quality) that inheres in it.

entities.label: InjusticeMoralQuality
entities.rationale: The property of being unjust, as attributed to a command, is a quality (specifically dependent continuant subtype BFO_0000019) that inheres in the command-as-GDC (or in the issuing institution/agent). It is distinct from the command's legal existence or formal validity.

entities.label: CommandIssuanceProcess
entities.rationale: The act of issuing a command is an occurrent — a process (BFO_0000015). The command-as-GDC is concretized in this process. Separating the process of issuance from the informational artifact (the command) maintains BFO coherence.

relations.rationale: InjusticeMoralQuality is a subclass of BFO Quality (BFO_0000019), as it is a measurable/evaluable property that inheres in a bearer.
An UnjustCommand is a subclass of generically dependent continuant — it is information content that can be multiply instantiated and is the bearer of an InjusticeMoralQuality.
CommandIssuanceProcess is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015) — the occurrent in which the command-GDC is concretized and transmitted.
An unjust command, when institutionally issued, is a species of LegalForm (already in working ontology as a GDC) — it has normative structure even when morally defective.

open_questions: Should 'command' here be restricted to legally authoritative commands (issued by a legal institution bearing CourtAuthority or similar role), or does it include informal moral commands and orders outside legal systems?

Is the injustice quality grounded in deviation from natural law norms (aligning with NaturalLawTheory) or simply in the violation of some independent moral standard? This affects whether InjusticeMoralQuality should be related to LegalLegitimacyCondition or kept purely evaluative.

Should UnjustCommand be distinguished from an 'invalid command' (one lacking legal existence conditions) per the existing LegalExistenceCondition / LegalLegitimacyCondition distinction already in the ontology? An unjust command may still be legally existent but lack legitimacy.
Is the bearer of InjusticeMoralQuality the command-as-GDC itself, or the LegalInstitution that issues it, or both? BFO requires qualities to inhere in exactly one bearer.
Should we reuse or relate UnjustCommand to the existing individual NaziRacialStatutes and its UnjustLegalSystemRole to maintain coherence with prior modeling?
proposal.rationale_summary: An unjust command in BFO terms is best analyzed as a generically dependent continuant (GDC, BFO_0000031) — an informational artifact (normative content) that can be concretized in multiple physical carriers — bearing an InjusticeMoralQuality (a Quality, BFO_0000019) that inheres in it. This mirrors the existing ontology's separation of LegalExistenceCondition (disposition grounding legal being) from LegalLegitimacyCondition (disposition grounding moral-legal authority): an unjust command can satisfy existence conditions while failing legitimacy conditions, consistent with the InjusticeDeprivesLegitimacyNotExistencePrinciple individual already in the graph. The act of issuing the command is modeled separately as a CommandIssuanceProcess (BFO_0000015), in which the command-GDC is concretized and the issuing agent participates. UnjustCommand is typed as a subclass of LegalForm to capture its formal normative structure. Three new classes are proposed: UnjustCommand (GDC), InjusticeMoralQuality (Quality), and CommandIssuanceProcess (Process). Several open questions remain about the scope of 'command,' the grounding of the injustice quality, and its exact bearer.
